messages:
maria.chen: Heads-up — discovered a set of tenant snapshots in s3://redwood-tenant-archives/tenant-1234/ that lack SSE-KMS metadata. Looks like objects are not tagged as encrypted at rest.
aj: :eyes: how many objects and when were they written?
maria.chen: ~42 objects, all written between 2026-03-18T02:10Z and 2026-03-18T02:22Z by backup job 'tenant-archiver'. enc-bot ran a scan and flagged them.
enc-bot: automated-scan: 42 objects missing x-amz-server-side-encryption header; severity=high; group=tenant-1234; suggested-action=manual re-encrypt + RBAC review
nate: Important — which IAM role performed the upload?
maria.chen: role=arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/backup-runner-prod. Looking at the role policy it currently has kms:Decrypt but not kms:Encrypt on the CMK (arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111111111111:key/cmk-0a1b2c).
ryan: That aligns with the RBAC hardening we applied last month — we removed broad kms:Encrypt from cross-account roles. Possible regression where the backup job didn't get its encryption permissions.
tasha: I'll take point on remediation. Plan: 1) limit blast radius — create a time-limited role 'snapshot-reencrypt' with kms:Encrypt scoped to cmk-0a1b2c and only allow from backup-runner-prod's session, 2) run a re-encrypt job, 3) audit logs + postmortem. Need thumbs-up.
aj: Before granting anything, confirm no object downloads or GetObject events in CloudTrail for these keys. If objects were exfiltrated, different response.
ir-oncall: IR opened: INC-2026-0318-ENC-1. Triage notes: no public access on bucket, no unusual s3:GetObject in last 30 days for tenant-1234. Marking moderate-severity pending audit log confirmation.
maria.chen: Quick CloudTrail grep shows PutObject events from backup-runner-prod at those times, no GetObject events. But S3 server access logs aren't enabled for that prefix — switching on now to get full request metadata.
ryan: Good. Also check KMS Key Usage logs. If the CMK didn't see GenerateDataKey/Encrypt events at that time, it's likely uploads were plaintext or used SSE-S3.
ate: Suggest we run a one-time re-encrypt using the documented pattern. Minimal downtime: stream-copy each object with metadata-directive REPLACE to set SSE-KMS. Example CLI we will run in a locked session:
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-tenant-archives/tenant-1234/ s3://redwood-tenant-archives/tenant-1234/ --recursive --metadata-directive REPLACE --server-side-encryption aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111111111111:key/cmk-0a1b2c
```
Note: we will run against a temp role with kms:Encrypt and s3:PutObject.
tasha: I'll provision the temp role with a 2-hour TTL and a CloudTrail event-based approval. Policy will include conditions: StringEquals aws:PrincipalTag/role=backup-runner-prod and DateLessThan to expire.
aj: Also add an S3 Bucket policy on the archive bucket to Deny PutObject if x-amz-server-side-encryption is missing unless caller is service-account backup-runner-prod. That prevents future regressions.
ryan: And update the KMS key policy so only specific roles can call Encrypt/GenerateDataKey. Remove the old wildcard principals. Add condition kms:CallerAccount and kms:EncryptionContext: { "tenant":"<tenant-id>" } if we can ensure the job sets it.
maria.chen: For immediate triage I will: 1) run CloudTrail and KMS logs export to the audit bucket, 2) enable S3 server access logs on archive bucket, 3) kick off re-encrypt job after tasha finishes role.
ir-oncall: Logging decisions saved on incident. We need a vulnerability triage entry: root cause likely RBAC policy change removed kms:Encrypt from backup role. Action items: short-term re-encrypt, medium-term enforce bucket put restrictions and key policy, long-term add CI test for backup job permission matrix.
aj: Create a JIRA: SEC-ENC-387 with owner @tasha, due EOD tomorrow for remediation tasks + postmortem doc. Include checklist: evidence of no exfil, list of affected objects, re-encrypt runbook, RBAC diff, key policy diff.
tasha: Created SEC-ENC-387 and linked to INC-2026-0318-ENC-1. I'll post the runbook and note the temp-role ARN once ready.
maria.chen: One more note — tenant escrow metadata (the sidecar JSON we store for tenant snapshots) didn't record encryption status because archive writer didn't validate SSE header. I'll patch the writer to assert SSE headers and fail uploads without it.
ryan: That's critical. Add a deploy gate for that patch and a unit test that simulates an IAM policy change and fails the upload in CI.
ate: After re-encrypt, we should run a verification job to assert all objects in tenant-1234 report SSE-KMS in HEAD object responses. I'll schedule it.
enc-bot: follow-up-scan scheduled in 1h to re-check tenant-1234 after re-encrypt job completes.
ir-oncall: Closing loop for now — put any new findings in the JIRA. Postmortem owner assigned to tasha. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
